title: Host diversity and adaptive vector feeding preferences shape disease burden in vector-borne diseases
summary: Vector-borne diseases often involve multiple host species that differ in their ability to sustain transmission. At the same time, vector feeding preferences can change in response to host availability and disease-control interventions, potentially altering disease dynamics in unexpected ways. We develop a two-host vector-borne disease model that links host diversity, adaptive vector feeding preferences, and disease transmission.
